title: APPROVAL OF HARBOR COMMUNITY BENEFIT FOUNDATION'S COMMUNITY BENEFIT GRANT PROGRAM, ROUND 10, SELECTION OF TEN ORGANIZATIONS TO RECEIVE GRANT AWARDS AND TRANSFER OF FUNDS FROM THE PORT COMMUNITY MITIGA
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVAL OF HARBOR COMMUNITY BENEFIT FOUNDATION'S COMMUNITY BENEFIT GRANT PROGRAM, ROUND 10, SELECTION OF TEN ORGANIZATIONS TO RECEIVE GRANT AWARDS AND TRANSFER OF FUNDS FROM THE PORT COMMUNITY MITIGATION TRUST FUND
Transmittal 1
Summary
: Staff requests that the Board of Harbor Commissioners (Board) approve the Harbor Community Benefit Foundation (HCBF) selection of ten (10) organizations to receive awards from the Community Benefit Grant Program, Round 10, and grant HCBF authority to disburse $1,000,000 from the Port Community Mitigation Trust Fund (PCMTF) to these grantees, following Board approval of the transfer of $1,000,000 from the PCMTF to HCBF. The PCMTF was established by the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department) for the purpose of funding appropriate mitigation projects and grants addressing port-related impacts for the communities of San Pedro and Wilmington. The HCBF, an independent nonprofit organization, is responsible for identifying qualifying projects to receive funding from the PCMTF, subject to approval by the Board. The HCBF Board of Directors has selected ten (10) organizations to receive funding for the tenth round (Round 10) of the Community Benefit Grant Program and is requesting Board approval of the award recipients and the transfer of $1,000,000 from the PCMTF, in accordance with the requirements of the TraPac Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) and Operating Agreement of the TraPac MOU (Operating Agreement). HCBF represents that all ten proposed projects have a Tidelands nexus and will mitigate, reduce, and address the Port of Los Angeles' (Port) impact on the local communities of Wilmington and San Pedro. Approval of this action will authorize the Harbor Community Benefit Foundation to disburse $1,000,000 to the 10 grantees approved hereunder from funds transferred to HCBF by JPMorgan Chase from the PCMTF for Round 10 Community Benefit Grants. The Harbor Department funded the original PCMTF. No additional payments from the Harbor Department will be required to fund this request. This program is in alignment with Strategic Objective 4: Strong Relationships with Stakeholders.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) approve the ten (10) organizations selected by the Harbor Community Benefit Foundation to receive awards from the Community Benefit Grant Program, Round 10, funded by the Port Community Mitigation Trust Fund:
(i) $120,000 to Braid Theory Impact,
(ii) $155,100 to California Benefits Support Center,
(iii) $97,000 to CHOICE Health Network,
(iv) $62,860 to International Bird Rescue,
(v) $72,860 to Los Angeles Maritime Institute (LAMI),
(vi) $125,000 to Memorial Medical Center Foundation (Miller Children's & Women's Hospital),
(vii) $29,000 to Port of Los Angeles High School,
(viii) $90,000 to St. Mary Medical Center Foundation,
(ix) $48,500 to Think Earth Environmental Education Foundation, and
(x) $199,680 to Wilmington Community Clinic;
3) approve the transfer of $1,000,000 from the Port Community Mitigation Trust Fund to the Harbor Community Benefit Foundation in a single lump sum, by authorizing the Executive Director or designee to execute a joint authorization letter to JPMorgan Chase, jointly executed by (a) the Board or its designee, and (b) an authorized Board representative of HCBF; 4) authorize the Harbor Community Benefit Foundation to disburse $1,000,000 to the ten (10) grantees approved hereunder from the funds transferred to HCBF pursuant to Item 3 above, consistent with HCBF's May 20, 2026 funding request; and 5) adopt Resolution No. __________.
Information Technology
summary: Approval of Harbor Community Benefit Foundation grant awards totaling $1,000,000 to ten organizations serving San Pedro and Wilmington communities.
